disposition_reason: Exposure assessment built on pooled means of published brown-vs-white rice studies; no new measurements. Table 4 unit label (µg/kg) is inconsistent with the magnitudes (mg/kg).

study.design: Literature compilation and exposure estimate using US NHANES 'What We Eat in America' rice intake
study.origin: Mixed: studies worldwide, and a US-focused subset
study.method: Not applicable (compilation of published studies with differing methods)

controls.control: Choosing white (milled) rice instead of brown rice
controls.comparator: Brown rice versus white rice, US-focused studies (pooled means)
controls.outcome: tAs 0.278 -> 0.244 (-12%), iAs 0.138 -> 0.093 (-33%) going from brown to white; equivalently brown is +14% tAs and +48% iAs versus white. Percentages computed from printed pooled means; unit printed as ug/kg, likely mg/kg.

controls.control: Choosing white (milled) rice instead of brown rice
controls.comparator: Brown rice versus white rice, worldwide pooled means
controls.outcome: tAs 0.277 -> 0.231 (-17%), iAs 0.163 -> 0.136 (-17%) going from brown to white; brown is +20% tAs and +20% iAs versus white. Percentages computed from printed pooled means.

controls.comparator: Rice bran versus white rice endosperm, worldwide pooled means
controls.outcome: Bran tAs 2.148 vs white 0.231 and bran iAs 1.769 vs white 0.136 (about 9-fold and 13-fold, computed); the authors state bran has 72.2%-98.3% higher inorganic arsenic than white rice.

controls.comparator: US-focused studies versus global pooled studies, inorganic share of total As
controls.outcome: iAs share of tAs 33% (US) vs 53% (global) for white rice and 48% (US) vs 65% (global) for brown rice; US pooled iAs 0.093 vs global 0.136 for white rice.

controls.control: Rice type chosen for young children (brown versus white)
controls.comparator: Brown versus white rice intake among children 6-24 months
controls.outcome: Authors' calculation: eaters-only iAs intake from brown rice 0.295 ug/kg bw/day versus 0.140 from white rice at 6-24 months, using the pooled US means (derived, not measured).

unresolved: Unit mislabeled in Table 4 (ug/kg vs likely mg/kg).
Text value 0.224 for US white rice tAs conflicts with Table 4 value 0.244.
Per-study rows in Table 4 not extracted (other authors' data); number of studies in each pooled mean not stated.
Several per-study iAs% values exceed 100 (e.g. 113 for bran) or iAs exceeds tAs (Naito et al. 2015 white rice iAs 0.683 vs tAs 0.250) in the compilation.
Exposure tables 7-8 are derived estimates and not extracted.
11 pooled literature means removed: Table 4 averages values from earlier studies (not new measurements) and labels them µg/kg although the magnitudes (e.g. US white rice tAs 0.244) are mg/kg.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: FDA action level for inorganic arsenic in infant rice cereal (2020)
JECFA 2001 inorganic arsenic limits for husked and polished rice (as cited)
Mean rice intake, eaters only, 6-24 months (WWEIA)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: brown 2.14 g/kg bw/day; white 1.51 g/kg bw/day (24-60 months white 1.55)
